# Multi-paragraph glossary placeholder reference

Original XML/OPC fixture generated by `tools/multiparagraph_placeholder_fixture.py`.
It contains two persistent block controls sharing a two-paragraph glossary prompt.
One starts with ordinary content; the other displays the prompt. No corpus text
or artwork is redistributed. Arial is referenced, not bundled.

`tools/record_multiparagraph_placeholder.ps1` records the reference application.
It deletes the filled control's contents, replaces the showing control with text,
then deletes that replacement. Both retain their wrapper, restore two paragraphs,
and set `showingPlcHdr`. Bold and italic prompt run formatting is restored.

Paragraph properties are context-dependent in these range edits. The filled
control restores both paragraphs without the glossary's paragraph properties.
The initially showing control retains the second paragraph's 360-twip indent,
but the first paragraph's 160-twip after-spacing is absent after replacement and
restoration. The PDFs/PNGs were visually reviewed and saved XML inspected. These
cases establish range-edit results, not all interactive keyboard behavior and
not a demonstrated specification divergence.

`native-typed.docx` and `native-reopened-restored.docx` confirm the same result after
saving and reopening the entered value: the final paragraph retains its indent,
while the newly restored preceding paragraph has no direct paragraph properties.

The editor now imports paragraph-only definitions for block controls and restores
their separate runs and paragraph boundaries. Inline controls still reject
multi-paragraph definitions. Other structural controls retain their guards.

`hashes.json` identifies the source and native artifacts. Both DOCX files pass
the repository's supported XML schema checks; that is not full conformance.
